quote: Culp, H. Lawrence Chairman & CEO ... Angel, Stephen F. Independent Director ... Goren, Isabella Davidov Independent Director ... Lesjak, Catherine A. Independent Director ... Horton, Thomas W. Lead Independent Director ... Bazin, Sebastien Marie Christophe Independent Director ... Billson, Margaret S. Independent Director ... Enders, Thomas Independent Director ... Garden, Edward Patrick Independent Director ... McDew, Darren Wayne Independent Director
finding: As of November 2025 the board is ten: Culp as combined Chairman and CEO plus nine independent directors, with Tom Horton as Lead Independent Director.

doc: S&P Capital IQ company profile, General Electric Company (GE Aerospace), printed 19 Nov 2025

quote: Total Revenue 43,950.0 Market Capitalization 312,235.5 ... Net Income 8,062.0 Total Debt 21,921.0 ... Issuer Credit Rating (Local Currency LT) A- Mar-25-2025 Stable
finding: On Capital IQ's November 2025 data, GE Aerospace has LTM revenue of about $44bn, net income of about $8.1bn, total debt of about $21.9bn and a $312bn market value, with a single-A-minus S&P rating, stable outlook (March 2025). Keeping the company in the A range is a standing financial-policy goal the board guards (CX-0252, CX-0659).

doc: S&P Capital IQ company profile, General Electric Company (GE Aerospace), printed 19 Nov 2025

quote: Shares Out. (mm) 1,054.8 Previous Close 296.01 Float % 99.6% ... The Teamster Affiliates Pension Plan, The Vanguard Group, Inc., Trian Fund Management, L.P.
finding: GE Aerospace is widely held (99.6% float, about 1.05bn shares) with index funds and the former activist Trian among listed investors; there is no state or controlling holder.

doc: GE Aerospace 2024 Annual Meeting of Shareholders
speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Our director nominees are Steve Angel, Chairman and former CEO of Linde, a director since 2022. Steve is Chair of the Management Development and Compensation Committee. ... Bella Goren, former CFO of American Airlines and AMR Corporation, a Director since 2022. Bella chairs our Audit Committee. Tom Horton, partner at Global Infrastructure Partners and the former Chairman and CEO of American Airlines, a Director since 2018. Tom is our Lead Director. Cathy Lesjak, former CFO of HP, a Director since 2019. Cathy is the Chair of the Governance and Public Affairs Committee. ... to serve as directors for the coming year, the 10 individuals who were introduced at the start of the meeting
finding: At the first GE Aerospace AGM the board was 10, with three standing committees (Compensation, Audit, Governance and Public Affairs) chaired by Angel, Goren and Lesjak, and Horton as Lead Director.

doc: GE Aerospace 2024 Annual Meeting of Shareholders
speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Sebastien Bazin Chairman and CEO of AccorHotels, a director since 2016; Peg Billson, former President and CEO of BBA Aviation's Global Engine Services Division, a Director since December of last year. Tom Enders, former CEO of Airbus, also a Director since December of 2023. Ed Garden, Chairman and CEO, Garden Investments, a director since 2017. ... Darren McDew retired, 4-star General United States Air Force and former Commander of the U.S. Transportation Command, a Director since 2023.
finding: The board added aerospace domain in 2023: an engine-services executive (Billson), a former Airbus CEO (Enders) and a retired four-star USAF general (McDew); Bazin is a hotel-group CEO and Garden the former Trian partner who joined in 2017.

doc: GE Aerospace 2024 Annual Meeting of Shareholders
speaker: John Chevedden (shareholder proposal); John R. Phillips, SVP & General Counsel (Board recommendation)
quote: Proposal requests that the Board of Directors adopt a joint policy and amend the governing documents in order that 2 separate people hold the office of Chairman and the office of the CEO. ... The Board recommends against this proposal for the reasons set forth on Page 61 of the proxy statement.
finding: The board keeps the combined Chairman-and-CEO role and, at the 2024 meeting, recommended against a shareholder proposal for an independent chair, relying on a Lead Director instead.

doc: GE Aerospace 2024 Annual Meeting of Shareholders
speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: one of the real opportunities that was presented was to build fit-for- purpose Boards each of the 3 and to add domain expertise and experience at the Board level ... almost half of our directors have engineering backgrounds, spanning aeronautical, astronomical, civil and chemical engineering backgrounds. Collectively, our directors also bring a wealth of leadership experience from across our sector, including airlines, airframers and defense customers
finding: The board was deliberately rebuilt for aerospace: about half engineers, with airline, airframer and defence-customer experience, so it can judge engine programmes on technical grounds.

doc: GE Aerospace 2024 Annual Meeting of Shareholders
speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Earlier this month, we initiated a quarterly dividend at $0.28, a mere 250% increase and a roughly 30% payout ratio. At our Investor Day, we also announced a $15 billion share buyback, a testament to the strength of our balance sheet. So combined dividends and share buybacks will each be about 4x where we were just last year.
finding: After the April 2024 spin the board approved a 30%-payout dividend and a $15bn buyback, quadrupling cash returns.

doc: GE Aerospace 2024 Annual Meeting of Shareholders
speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: So for GE Aerospace as a standalone company, the Board, our leadership team and the entire team are really focused on our commercial and defense customers and our industry stakeholders. ... Short term, with FLIGHT DECK as our foundation, we will use problem-solving to break constraints like challenged supply chains, all the while enhancing safety, quality, delivery and cost, again, in that order.
finding: The board's stated focus is customers, with safety ranked first in the fixed order safety, quality, delivery, cost.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Thank you for your patience and giving us the time and space to work this through with the Board. We're excited to share this framework with you today. As you might imagine, first things first, we're going to reinvest in the business, be that in R&D, be that in CapEx. That will be the first order.
finding: The capital allocation framework was set with the board, and its first priority is reinvestment in R&D and capex, ahead of cash returns.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: allocation was going to be a key responsibility for not only the management team, but the Board. And I think any current holders, any future holders would have been delighted with the Board conversation on that topic last week in Dallas. I think our framework, David, really is unchanged. We've said we're going to have a bias, first and foremost to make sure we protect the organic investments that we make in the business, principally R&D. We're not going to target a fixed ratio at any point in time, but you'll see that R&D as a percent of sales fluctuate in the 6% to 8% range
finding: Capital allocation is a board responsibility; the board protects organic R&D first, at about 6-8% of sales, before buybacks or M&A.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: As we go forward, we're clearly going to continue down this path of returning capital to shareholders, again, $6 billion last year, $8 billion this year, in excess of our cash flow. Now that will be hard to continue into perpetuity, of course, but that will be the bias.
finding: The board's bias is to return more than 100% of free cash flow in the near term: a short-term pull that sits alongside the R&D protection.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Last week, we had our Board together in Dallas for a couple of days. We had a few customers come in. So a really good opportunity to go deep on our commercial engine strategy.
finding: The board holds multi-day strategy sessions with customers present to go deep on commercial engine strategy.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: the capital allocation approach that we and the Board have taken since the spin is very much intact. ... first and foremost, making sure we're reinvesting in the business to drive technology improvements ... investors should continue to see from us a disciplined approach where we really look to strategic fit, then operational value add and in turn, financial returns. ... organic reinvestment, return of capital to shareholders will be the first 2 priorities.
finding: As of October 2025 the board's ranking is unchanged: organic reinvestment first, cash returns second, then disciplined M&A screened on strategic fit, operational value and returns.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We're just in the process of wrapping up our strategy reviews. We'll spend the fourth quarter working through the details of the '26 budget. ... We'll take the Board through it at the end of the year, and then we'll come back in earnings and talk about '26 in more detail is basically our practice here.
finding: The annual strategy reviews and budget go to the board each year end before guidance is given: the board's yearly approval cycle.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And given the strength of our balance sheet, we're increasing our share repurchases to $7 billion and planned to raise our dividend by 30%, subject, of course, to board approval.
finding: Buyback and dividend increases are board decisions, announced by management as subject to board approval.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I think what we've always tried to do is really adhere to a handful of principles with respect to making sure we share in the value that we create, are compensated for the risks that we take on and obviously deliver adequate returns on the investments, the long-term, long-cycle investments that we make.
finding: The pricing and investment principle: take risk only when compensated, and earn adequate returns on long-cycle investments.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Safety is and always will be foundational to everything we do. ... GE Aerospace was the first manufacturer to have a Safety Management System, or SMS, accepted by the FAA. We established our SMS a decade before the agency proposed requiring it. ... SMS, together with our Quality Management System are the foundation of our safety culture
finding: Safety is run through an FAA-accepted Safety Management System (the first accepted from a manufacturer) and a Quality Management System; said a month after the Air India 171 accident (see CX-0648).

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: As a general matter, we do like to maintain a relatively small Board because it enables us to be both nimble when we need to act and also to engage in depth conversations as a whole group. ... We like our current size of 10 directors ... Based on the Board's self- evaluations, comparing Board size of peers and investor feedback, we think the GE Board and eventually the spin-off company Boards will continue to be approximately the same size.
finding: A deliberately small board of about 10, so that it can act quickly and debate as a whole group, sized by self-evaluation and investor feedback.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: it's our Board that oversees the execution of GE's sustainability priorities and initiatives as part of an integrated -- as an integrated part of our overall strategy and risk management.
finding: The board owns risk oversight and treats sustainability as part of strategy and risk management; RISE's fuel-burn goals fall under it (inference).

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: The boardroom conversations are fundamentally different than they were just a few years ago, right? We've now reduced our debt load by $100 billion. ... So we have a lot of options. And I would say all options are on the table. However, job 1 remains: The completion of what we announced
finding: Deleveraging changed the board's conversation from survival to choice, but finishing the announced plan still came first.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: the overarching priority, making sure we send all 3 of the businesses out with IG ratings. ... And we want to make sure we give the Board all the ample support and space to work through those opportunities, those priorities to take the right decisions at the right time. The buyback that the Board actioned on Sunday was really to set up the authorization to be clear, was really to set up, again, that option amongst many.
finding: At the break-up, sending all three companies out with investment-grade ratings was the overarching priority, and buyback authority was a board action that created an option rather than a commitment to spend.

doc: GE special call: plan to form three public companies
speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: GE will then become an Aviation-focused company, shaping the future of flight. This plan is the result of a thoughtful, deliberate strategic process by our Board of Directors and senior management team.
finding: The board decided in November 2021 to break GE into three companies, leaving GE Aerospace as the remaining company.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And our Board was together again last week, Josh, it's a heck of a Board, a Board very keen as we get past the deleveraging to make sure we're reinvesting at every turn, both organically and inorganically into the business.
finding: Once deleveraging was done, the board pressed for reinvestment in the business, not only for cash returns.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: this Board is going to be hyper focused as well on making sure that we evaluate any and all options to create shareholder value. We want to do that in a thoughtful, rational, considered way. We can do that more so today than we could 3 years ago given the balance sheet progress
finding: The board's style is to weigh every option in a 'thoughtful, rational, considered way', with freedom of action tied to balance-sheet strength.

speaker: Thomas W. Horton, Lead Independent Director and Chair, Management Development and Compensation Committee
quote: With the onset of the COVID pandemic and the challenges that has posed, it became abundantly clear to us as the Board that GE's transformation would take longer than planned. At our board discussions in 2020, we spent a lot of time on risk oversight related to COVID and the effects it was having on GE. ... One of the most important actions we took as a board, as described in the proxy and elsewhere, was extending the term of Larry's employment agreement so that GE would have his continued leadership through at least 2024.
finding: In 2020 the board's response to COVID was risk oversight and leadership continuity: it extended Culp's contract to at least 2024.

speaker: Thomas W. Horton, Lead Independent Director and Chair, Management Development and Compensation Committee
quote: The way we viewed it as a Board was as an extension of Larry's leadership through at least 2024 with a corresponding change to the accompanying grant that keeps Larry's compensation overwhelmingly tied to GE's performance. ... The performance share target a significant return to the shareholders that represents an increase in GE's market capitalization in the range of $26 billion to $78 billion.
finding: The board ties CEO pay to multi-year share-price performance (a grant measured to 2024), so the pay horizon is several years and is stock-price based.

speaker: Thomas W. Horton, Lead Independent Director and Chair, Management Development and Compensation Committee
quote: GE's compensation program is designed to incentivize and hold management accountable for executing on the business strategy. ... As one example, the annual performance equity grants in 2018 and 2019 fell short of their targets and resulted in no payout.
finding: The compensation committee lets performance grants lapse when targets are missed (2018 and 2019 paid nothing).

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: clawbacks would come into play in a case of serious misconduct as opposed to business decisions that did not go as anticipated. We've now had a thorough review led by a special committee of our Board working with outside independent counsel, and the Board concluded that the company has no sound legal basis to see clawbacks or pursue litigation.
finding: The board separates misconduct from failed business bets: after a special-committee review it did not claw back pay for decisions that went wrong.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: No, I serve at the Board's pleasure, and I was gratified that they wanted me to stay longer, witnessed the extension last summer.
finding: The CEO describes himself as serving at the board's pleasure, even while he chairs it.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: we have taken significant action over the last several years to reduce the size of the Board from a high of 18 directors in 2017 to the 11 nominees before you today, which is in line with the average board size for the S&P 500. Most of our director compensation is in the form of stock units that do not pay out until after a director retires.
finding: Directors are paid mostly in stock units that pay out only after they retire, which ties their own pay to the long-run share price.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And that is something that this management team and this Board is very keen to do, rest assured. But I think we're going to not try to get ahead of ourselves. At times, you might think we're being a little conservative. But again, we want to make sure we strengthen this company
finding: The board wanted to 'play offense' only after the balance sheet was fortified and admitted to looking conservative.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I joined the Board a year ago that was nearly 18 people large, right? Today as we sit here before you, we have 10 members of the board. ... But most importantly, this is a board that can have honest, candid, tough conversations. We had one at 8 o'clock just across the way.
finding: After the 2017-2018 crisis the board was cut from 18 to 10 and describes itself as willing to have tough, candid debates.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: But ultimately, there's a responsibility on all of us in the boardroom, right, to make sure we're making the tough, best, long-term decisions for our company in the best way that we know how.
finding: The board frames its duty as making the tough, long-term decisions.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: This isn't about the first quarter of this year. It's not even about this year. What we're really signed up to the team that we have both at the board level and at a management level, long- term value creation as we transform this industrial icon.
finding: The board and management are explicitly signed up to long-term value creation, not the quarter.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: In this role for 30 days, on the board for less than a year ... Frankly, I'm not sure, when my board colleagues came to me, that I would have stepped into this role hadn't I been out on the road over the course of the summer
finding: In October 2018 the board replaced the CEO with one of its own directors, an outsider who had joined the board in April 2018.

speaker: John L. Flannery, then Chairman & CEO
quote: We also have 3 new director nominees who will join the board after today's meeting. I'd like to introduce them as well, starting first with Larry Culp, who is the former President and CEO of Danaher; Tom Horton who's the former Chairman and CEO of American Airlines; and Leslie Seidman is the Former Chairman of the Financial Accounting Standards Board. I'd also like to acknowledge 8 directors of ours who are not standing for reelection ... You'll note that we're nominating a much smaller board this year. It was really based on a decision made by the board after its own self-assessment and also a lot of input from our investors.
finding: In April 2018 the board shrank itself after a self-assessment and investor input (eight directors did not stand) and brought in Culp, Horton and Seidman: Culp is today's chair-CEO and Horton was Lead Director from 2018 to September 2026 (CG-0041).

speaker: John L. Flannery, then CEO
quote: We've just appointed a committee of our Board, a new committee of our Board, the Finance and Capital Allocation Committee. And the first thing I've tasked them to work on is evaluating our exit options on Baker Hughes.
finding: In the 2017 crisis the board created a Finance and Capital Allocation Committee to review portfolio exits.

speaker: John L. Flannery, then CEO
quote: We announced last week that Ed Garden from Trian is joining the board. Things will not stay the same at GE.
finding: The activist Trian won a board seat (Ed Garden) in October 2017; he served until the May 2026 annual meeting, where he did not stand (CG-0044).
